skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray with bilateral opacities and pleural fluid to distinguish between cardiogenic pulmonary edema and infectious pneumonia.
steps: Assess the distribution of alveolar consolidations: check if opacities are symmetric and centered in the perihilar regions (bat-wing pattern) versus asymmetric, patchy, or lobar.
Evaluate the pleural spaces bilaterally: look for blunting of costophrenic angles or meniscus signs on both sides versus unilateral fluid collection.
Inspect the cardiac silhouette and mediastinum for cardiomegaly or vascular congestion supporting a cardiac etiology.

Synthesize findings: Bilateral perihilar consolidations combined with bilateral pleural effusions strongly suggest pulmonary edema due to cardiac failure, whereas asymmetric consolidation with unilateral effusion favors pneumonia.
